item.title: Federal judge rules Trump admin plan to cut FEMA workforce in half is unlawful
item.description: A federal judge ruled DHS unlawfully seized the Federal Emergency Management Agency's authority over staffing and pushed thousands of job cuts.
item.content:encoded:
A federal judge ruled that the Trump administration's directive for the Federal Emergency Management Agency to cut its workforce in half was unlawful.

U.S. District Judge Susan Illston found on Friday that the Department of Homeland Security acted unlawfully by taking control of FEMA's authority over its own personnel and pushing the agency to slash thousands of disaster-response jobs.

Although FEMA is under DHS, a federal law adopted after Hurricane Katrina in 2005 states that the department "may not substantially or significantly reduce (FEMA's) authorities, responsibilities, or functions."

Illston said the department violated the law last year when it sought to stop FEMA from renewing the temporary contracts of thousands of on-call reservists who respond to disasters.

DHS PLANS COSTLY CRACKDOWN ON STATES THAT DON’T COOPERATE ON ELECTION SECURITY

"There is no evidence in the record reflecting reasoned decision-making for this about-face or for the subsequent conditions DHS placed on FEMA’s renewal authority," Illston wrote.

Illston's ruling did not include remedies or penalties, noting that those would be addressed in a separate ruling next month.

The judge said the parties have until Oct. 9 to submit briefings on "what relief remains outstanding" in this case.

The unions that sued argued that the planned cuts are unlawful because they would undermine FEMA's core disaster‑response mission, were not approved by Congress and were ordered by then-Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem instead of FEMA officials.

The administration has contended that FEMA has considerable flexibility to determine proper staffing levels. President Donald Trump has suggested that FEMA should ​be eliminated and that states ⁠should handle their emergency preparedness.

In June, Illston declined to immediately block the job cuts, ruling that FEMA had at least temporarily abandoned its planned layoffs.

But on Friday, the judge wrote that FEMA appeared to be moving forward with the job cuts. She said FEMA projected its staffing levels for the upcoming fiscal year at 11,383 employees, or about half of previous levels, without any basis for picking that figure.

DEM GOV LASHES OUT AS TRUMP HUD SCRUTINIZES NEARLY $2B IN DISASTER FUNDS OVER FRAUD CONCERNS

Fox News Digital reached out to DHS and FEMA for comment but they did not immediately respond.

"Under President Trump and [DHS] Secretary [Markwayne] Mullin’s leadership, DHS and FEMA are ready for the 2026 hurricane season," a FEMA spokesperson said in a statement to The Hill. "FEMA continues to maintain a roster of experienced leadership and support staff across headquarters and regional offices. No position is without experienced leadership."

In a separate ruling, the judge also faulted FEMA and DHS officials for using the Signal messaging app on their personal cell phones to discuss staffing cuts and deleting the messages.

Illston said the messages would have been relevant to the lawsuit and that she would now presume "that the lost Signal messages would have been unfavorable to Defendants because they would have been further evidence" of unlawful conduct.

Reuters contributed to this report.

item.title: John Harbaugh's Giants on full display in bruising win over Cowboys to kick off NFL season
item.description: Methodic runs, more mature Jaxson Dart, and chewing clock led to a perfect start to the John Harbaugh era for the New York Giants against the Dallas Cowboys.
item.content:encoded:
For months, the talk throughout the tri-state area had been about this new era for the New York Giants.

How could it not be, as John Harbaugh, after almost two decades with the Baltimore Ravens, signed on as the next Giants head coach. It was a post he said he felt pride assuming, understanding the expectations and pedigree he was supposed to bring back to a prestigious franchise that had been reeling until his arrival.

Well, the Harbaugh era kicked off in the best way possible for Giants fans on Sunday night, as they took down the Dallas Cowboys, 28-20, in the hard-nosed fashion that was to be expected with this new regime.

From the very beginning, the Giants’ defense forced a three-and-out and got a sold-out MetLife Stadium crowd on their feet as Jaxson Dart and company took the field for the first time in 2026. What ensued was a 10-play, 83-yard drive that took 6:13 off the first-quarter clock and resulted in a Cam Skattebo touchdown.

While Harbaugh may not have enjoyed Skattebo’s celebratory backflip, the 7-0 lead on the opening drive was exactly what this coaching staff wanted to see with its top offensive weapons out there for the first time this season.

Long drives were a theme for the Giants in this game, as they used a bruising run game, and some creative play-calls that came at the right time, to fluster the Cowboys’ defense, which was supposed to be an improved unit this season.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Instead, it looked like the Cowboys defense from last season, which struggled to match the power of the offense.

The Giants converted nine of its 11 third downs in this game, and though the Cowboys had eight of their 11 third downs that moved the chains, New York’s came at the right time it seemed on each drive as they methodically moved downfield to set themselves up for scores.

And two of those touchdowns came from Harbaugh’s past with the Ravens.

Isaiah Likely proved to be the catalyst many believed he could for the Giants this season, hauling in two of Dart’s 3 touchdown passes as he finished with a game-high 78 yards on eight receptions.

CAM SKATTEBO HORRIFIES GIANTS FANS BY ATTEMPTING A BACKFLIP DESPITE COMING OFF A LEG INJURY

Just behind him, though, was Malik Nabers, whom the Giants made sure to be cautious with up until gametime this week. Nabers suffered a torn ACL and more in Week 4 last season, and though he has been without a non-contact uniform during practice, Harbaugh wouldn’t tell anyone if he’d play on Sunday night.

Nabers got two thumbs up from trainers before the game, and after being deemed active, he finished with six catches for 69 yards in his return to the Giants, which led to smiles from himself, his teammates and coaches, and all 80,000-plus fans in the stands.

The night would’ve been wrapped up in a bow if Odell Beckham Jr. notched a statistic for the Giants, but that will have to wait for the coming weeks. Beckham, who made the 53-man roster out of training camp, was active but never saw a pass from Dart.

One of the reasons? The Harbaugh effect . A ground-and-pound, tough, physical run game that saw 37 carries that featured creatively from offensive coordinator Matt Nagy and run game coordinator Greg Roman that resulted in 165 rushing yards as a team compared to the Cowboys’ 69.

It’s one thing to think about what a new regime could look like before a season starts, but Harbaugh’s preaching about being a team that resembled the Giants of old that he grew up watching seemed to come to fruition, at least in some respect, on Sunday night in East Rutherford, New Jersey.

item.title: La Catalina ends Flammer's 1,128-day reign as AAA Reina de Reinas champion at Triplemania 34
item.description: Roxanne Perez already awaits as No. 1 contender after La Catalina ended Flammer's historic 1,128-day Reina de Reinas reign at Triplemania 34.
item.content:encoded:
La Catalina made her AAA debut in April to the surprise of Mexican fans and immediately worked her way into the Reina de Reinas Championship picture.

She won a gauntlet match to get a title shot at Triplemania 34, and on Sunday, she ended the long reign of Flammer to win the title.

COMPLETE PRO WRESTLING COVERAGE ON OUTKICK

La Catalina had Flammer on the ropes late in the match. She went for a diving splash but didn’t get all of it as Flammer put her knees up at the last second. Flammer avoid the pinfall at that point and thought she got back in control when she dropkicked La Catalina out of the ring.

Flammer looked up the ramp, appearing to wonder where La Hiedra was. La Hiedra, Flammer’s tag team partner, was nowhere to be found. It took Flammer out of her game. La Catalina tossed Flammer from the top rope. She nailed a hip attack and then a running knee to topple Flammer.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

The win for La Catalina ends Flammer’s illustrious title reign at 1,128 days. She was the longest-reigning Reina de Reinas champion and one of the longest-reigning champions across pro wrestling. But all of that ended in Mexico City on Night 2 of AAA’s premier events.

There will be no rest for the new champion as she already has a challenger waiting in the wings.

Roxanne Perez earned the No. 1 contender spot for the title on Night 1 of Triplemania 34. She held off Nattie, La Hiedra and Faby Apache to win the match. Perez pinned La Hiedra, who appeared to be hoping for Flammer to have her back in that match.

Whatever the disconnect was between Flammer and La Hiedra, it showed up on the biggest stage of Lucha Libre.

La Catalina and Perez will battle for the title at Worlds Collide later this month.

item.title: Giants honor 9/11 heroes before emotional Sunday Night Football opener against Cowboys
item.description: MetLife Stadium's 9/11 tribute before Giants vs. Dallas Cowboys featured the Tribute in Light, FDNY's Ladder 343 truck and a giant American flag.
item.content:encoded:
Before the Giants took to the field against the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday Night Football, MetLife Stadium marked the 25th anniversary of the Sept. 11 terrorist attacks with a pregame tribute honoring victims and first responders.

Fans arriving at MetLife Stadium were welcomed by FDNY’s ceremonial Ladder 343 truck and an authentic World Trade Center steel beam displayed outside the gates by the Tunnel to Towers Foundation.

Two vertical columns of light, echoing the World Trade Center’s "Tribute in Light," illuminated the night sky above MetLife Stadium.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

The ceremony included a special performance of the national anthem by members of the NYPD and FDNY.

On the field, players, coaches and Giants season-ticket members held a 100-yard wide American flag stretching from end zone to end zone.

New York City first responders formed a gauntlet for the Giants during player introductions. Players, coaches and staff from both teams wore commemorative NYPD, FDNY and PAPD hats on the sideline, while players and coaches wore "Never Forget" T-shirts during warm-ups.

NFL'S WEEK 1 9/11 TRIBUTE BEGINS IN SEATTLE WITH WILD GUITAR SOLO DURING NATIONAL ANTHEM

Members of the Palumbo family, whose FDNY father died on 9/11, served as honorary captains for the coin toss. A photo montage of lives lost on 9/11 played on the stadium’s video boards during a moment of silence.

Giants legends also joined uniformed first responders for the "Go Big Blue" chant before kickoff.

SON WHO LOST FATHER IN 9/11 ATTACKS SHARES POWERFUL LESSONS 25 YEARS LATER: ‘I’M STILL HERE’

For new Giants coach John Harbaugh, who took over after 18 seasons in Baltimore, the tribute carried special significance.

"It’s a story about heroes who were willing to run toward danger while others were trying to escape it," Harbaugh said. "To be in New York and honor the heroes of that day who live on forever in our culture, that means everything. You honor it with your effort."

JOHN HARBAUGH AND JAXSON DART AIM TO PULL THE NEW YORK GIANTS OUT OF THE NFC EAST BASEMENT

With Harbaugh in charge, the Giants believe better days are ahead.

item.title: Trump says China 'spies' on US after report ties Chinese imagery to Iran strike
item.description: The president said the U.S. spies on China "too" after a report linked Chinese satellite imagery to Iran's deadly July missile attack on American troops.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump said Sunday that China "spies on us" just as "we spy on them," following a report that Chinese entities provided Iran with satellite imagery before a deadly missile attack that killed three U.S. troops.

While speaking to reporters aboard Air Force One, Trump was asked about a Wall Street Journal report that Chinese entities allegedly supplied Iran with high-resolution satellite imagery of Muwaffaq Salti Air Base in Jordan before Tehran's July 17 missile attack.

"They basically do what we do," Trump said.

TRUMP GIVES SMITHSONIAN DAYS TO REPLACE 'STRANGE MODERNIST SCULPTURE' WITH FOUNDING FATHER

Asked whether he planned to raise the issue with Chinese President Xi Jinping when he visits the U.S., Trump said Xi has "behaved reasonably well," and that "we behave reasonably well."

"You know what they say? That China spies on us. I say you're right, and we spy on them, too," Trump said.

TRUMP TELLS ZELENSKYY TO STOP DOING 'ONE THING' DURING ATTACKS ON RUSSIA

According to The Wall Street Journal, U.S. officials linked the imagery to Iran's July 17 strike on the Jordanian base, which killed three U.S. troops. 

Officials described it as the clearest evidence to date that support from Chinese entities for Iran during the war has had deadly consequences for American forces, the outlet reported.

TRUMP SAYS HE WOULD 'LOVE' TO SEE IRELAND UNIFIED AS ONE NATION

The U.S. officials did not identify the Chinese entities involved or accuse Beijing of direct involvement in the attack. 

Xi is scheduled to visit Washington on Sept. 24 for a summit with Trump.

The White House could not immediately be reached by Fox News Digital for comment.

Fox News Digital's Emma Bussey contributed to this report.

item.title: California football coach arrested after students make disturbing discovery at school
item.description: The Tracy Unified School District placed the educator and football coach, Jeffrey Pribble, on leave as separate criminal and district investigations continue.
item.content:encoded:
A high school football coach in California was arrested Friday after students discovered a cellphone secretly recording them while they were changing inside a campus locker room, police said.

The phone belonged to Jeffrey Pribble, a 48-year-old teacher at Tracy High School, located east of San Francisco, the Tracy Police Department said Saturday.

According to the school's website and social media accounts, Pribble is the varsity football head coach and works in the school's physical education program.

Pribble has held the coaching position for five years and has 22 years of experience as an educator with the district, according to his Facebook page.

SCHOOL EMPLOYEE ACCUSED OF SECRETLY FILMING 12 GIRLS IN CHANGING ROOM FACES NEW CHARGES

The discovery was made Thursday when a student and several classmates found the phone recording inside the locker room, officials said.

The students stopped the recording, deleted the video and turned the device over to a teacher.

By Thursday evening, a concerned parent then contacted Tracy police patrol officers, prompting school resource officers and detectives to open an investigation.

The following day, officers determined that the phone belonged to Pribble, who was arrested Friday.

The Tracy Unified School District placed Pribble on leave pending the outcome of separate criminal and district investigations, officials said.

According to the Pleasanton Weekly, Tracy High Principal Jon Waggle acknowledged the arrest of an employee in an email to parents.

FLORIDA MIDDLE SCHOOL TEACHER ADMITS TO YEARS OF 'INAPPROPRIATE' CONVERSATIONS WITH FORMER STUDENT: DEPUTIES

The school did not identify the teacher or the specific allegations but noted that the district was fully cooperating with police.

"We understand that this news may raise serious concerns in the District community. The District too is concerned about the well-being of its students and staff and is committed to holding its employees to the highest professional and ethical standards," Waggle wrote.

"Tracy High School and all our Tracy Unified schools are proud of being safe schools. The cooperation between students, parents and staff members keeps our schools safe and is important and appreciated. Thank you for your continued partnership and support."

Tracy Police Chief Sekou Millington added that the safety and privacy of the city's students remain among the department's top priorities.

"Our children deserve to feel safe at school and in every space where they should be able to learn, grow, and simply be kids," Millington said.

"Protecting the safety, privacy, and well-being of our students is a responsibility we take seriously. We are grateful to the students who brought this incident to the attention of adults and to the officers and detectives who acted quickly to investigate."

Fox News Digital reached out to Tracy High School for more information.

item.title: Air Force colonel shot down over Iran reveals desperate prayer in 50-hour fight to survive
item.description: An Air Force colonel survived a 70-100 mph parachute fall into Iran with three broken bones and evaded enemy capture for 50 harrowing hours.
item.content:encoded:
An Air Force colonel shot down over Iran survived a terrifying fall, three broken bones and a two-day enemy manhunt after turning to God as his damaged parachute sent him plunging toward the desert.

The colonel, identified only by his mission call sign "Bravo," revealed in a new interview with CBS News’ "60 Minutes" how a desperate prayer began an extraordinary 50-hour fight to make it home alive.

"At one point when I looked up and saw no parachute, that was the most terrifying thing I’ve ever seen," Bravo said in his first public account of the April ordeal.

"So I paused, right then, and I prayed, ‘Lord, your will be done. But if I’m getting through this, I need help.’"

HOLLYWOOD LEGEND MAKING MOVIE ABOUT EPIC IRAN RESCUE MISSION TO SAVE F-15 FIGHTER JET CREW

The colonel was the weapons systems officer seated behind the pilot of an F-15E Strike Eagle operating under the call sign Dude 44 when an Iranian shoulder-fired missile struck the aircraft April 2, according to CBS News.

OPERATION EPIC FURY SHATTERED IRAN’S POWER, BUT EXPOSED RISKS AMERICA CAN’T IGNORE

The two-man crew had been assigned to attack industrial facilities tied to Iran’s drone and missile program near a mountainous region south of Isfahan, U.S. Central Command leader Adm. Brad Cooper told the outlet.

"We had air superiority, but clearly we weren’t flying over Kansas," Cooper said.

THE LEGACY OF 'EAGLE CLAW': HOW FAILURE HELPED BUILD AMERICA'S ELITE SPECIAL FORCES

Bravo described the missile strike as feeling like the jet had been hit by a freight train. He and the pilot, known as "Alpha," initially tried to save the roughly $30 million aircraft before realizing they had no choice but to eject.

Alpha escaped safely, but the missile had damaged Bravo’s parachute, sending him hurtling toward the ground at an estimated 70 to 100 mph, CBS reported.

SEAL TEAM 6 MEMBER REVEALS EPIC DETAILS OF OSAMA BIN LADEN RAID

The violent landing broke Bravo’s back, arm and shoulder and left him stranded roughly five miles from Alpha in the heart of enemy territory.

Despite his injuries, Bravo moved away from his landing site and began climbing toward a roughly 7,000-foot ridgeline as daylight revealed the desert valley and steep cliffs surrounding him.

SEAL TEAM 6 MEMBER EXPLAINS BLUNT REALITY OF COMBAT AND EXPECTATIONS IN THE BLACK OPS WORLD

"Never let a lack of motivation put you on Iranian TV," he told CBS.

Iranian forces were actively hunting the downed aviators and at one point came within several hundred meters of Bravo, according to U.S. military officials cited by the outlet. Images of the wrecked American fighter jet had already appeared in Iranian media, while videos reportedly showed armed groups searching the region.

PETE HEGSETH HEADS TO CAPITOL HILL TO DEFEND TRUMP'S IRAN WAR AS 60-DAY CONGRESSIONAL DEADLINE LOOMS

"There was clear intent out of the Iranian ground force to come find those two guys," Joint Chiefs of Staff Chairman Gen. Dan Caine told CBS.

Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said he was awakened in the middle of the night and informed that the fighter jet had been shot down.

"Whether they’re alive or not, we’re going to go get them," Hegseth recalled.

American forces rescued Alpha about six hours after the crash during a dangerous daylight mission in which U.S. helicopters came under fire.

"It was a gun fight all the way in and all the way out," Hegseth said. "But they got Alpha back."

Bravo, however, could not be found.

TRUMP OPENS HORMUZ UNDER FIRE WITH ‘PROJECT FREEDOM’ AS IRAN WARNS OF ATTACKS

In a statement provided to "60 Minutes," Alpha praised the combat search-and-rescue teams and other U.S. forces involved in bringing both men home.

"Words cannot capture how thankful my family and I are and how proud I am to serve alongside each and every one of them," Alpha said.

The pilot has since returned to flying but declined to appear publicly because of security concerns, CBS reported.

As darkness fell on Bravo’s first day in Iran, the injured colonel managed to send a message to U.S. forces.

"God is good," he wrote.

Bravo also told commanders that he was injured but still moving. Military leaders considered launching another rescue operation that night, but Hegseth said the conditions did not come together and officials made the agonizing decision to leave the colonel in Iran for another day.

Bravo endured the high desert’s wind and cold with almost no food or water while American forces tracked both him and the Iranian teams trying to capture him.

The CIA launched a deception campaign designed to confuse Iranian forces and used classified technology to pinpoint Bravo’s location, according to CBS. Newly declassified footage showed U.S. bombers and drones striking nearby forces linked to Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps as the rescue mission moved into place.

More than 90 U.S. service members entered Iran on the ground, marking the first American boots inside the country in 46 years, Cooper told the outlet. Hundreds more took part in the air, while thousands provided support.

Two large search-and-rescue aircraft landed on a makeshift desert runway before smaller "Little Bird" helicopters flew toward Bravo’s position on the ridgeline.

Bravo called the moment he saw his rescuers "one of the greatest moments of my life."

His first words to them were simple: "Let’s go."

But the dangerous operation was not over.

TRUMP SAYS US WILL 'BEAT THE F------ S--- OUT OF THEM' AFTER IRAN LAUNCHES SURPRISE MISSILE STRIKE

The landing gear of the two rescue planes became trapped in the desert sand, stranding Bravo and more than 90 elite U.S. service members. A clandestine Air Force unit was ultimately brought in to extract the group, CBS reported.

The U.S. military then destroyed the two stranded aircraft, each valued at roughly $100 million, along with the smaller helicopters to prevent sensitive American technology from falling into Iranian hands.

Bravo was finally safe about 50 hours after Dude 44 was shot down, with the rescue completed as the sun rose on Easter Sunday.

The colonel, who called his survival a "modern-day miracle," said he believes God carried him through the fall and the harrowing days that followed.

"I believe that it’s a testament to God’s provision in my life to bring me through that moment in a way that didn’t prevent injuries, but prevented any catastrophic injuries that would have affected my ability to survive," he told CBS.

Bravo said his ordeal was ultimately bigger than one downed aviator.

"It’s a story of the teamwork, the training, of the faith, of the decisions and the leadership to do something that will live in history as an example of what America’s willing to do, in order to uphold our promise and leave no man behind."

Bravo's first public account aired during the season premiere of CBS News' "60 Minutes," marking the start of the program's first season under editor-in-chief Bari Weiss and executive producer Nick Bilton.

item.title: Maryland dad blamed 'Satan' after 2-month-old daughter died from horrific head trauma
item.description: A Maryland father blamed "Satan" for his 2-month-old daughter's fatal head trauma that led to her death, as he and the child's mother are facing child abuse charges.
item.content:encoded:
A Maryland couple was arrested after the death of their 2-month-old daughter who suffered head injuries, with the father allegedly telling police the girl's injuries were caused by "Satan slamming a door on the child," according to charging documents and prosecutors.

Oscar Pineda and Katerin Monzon-Alvarado, both 21, are facing charges for first and second-degree child abuse, first and second-degree assault and reckless endangerment that carry a maximum possible sentence of 55 years in prison in connection with the death of 2-month-old Aida Mikea Monzon Alvarado, Baltimore Police said, adding that they could face additional homicide charges pending the outcome of the autopsy report.

The baby was taken to Harbor Hospital on Wednesday with what doctors described as "suspicious" severe bruising around her eyes and jawline. A later examination revealed what charging documents describe as "significant head and brain trauma" and "multiple skull fractures" that were not noticed during the initial examination, charging documents state, according to CBS Baltimore.

IDAHO MOM WHO CLAIMED VACCINES KILLED HER TWIN BABIES CHARGED WITH MURDERING HER KIDS

The girl's father allegedly claimed to police that his daughter was injured "due to a supernatural force or Satan slamming a door on the child." The mother said her 2-year-old son often jumps on the bed, which caused the baby to fall onto the floor, a prosecutor said at a court hearing on Friday, according to the outlet.

The prosecutor argued that the extent of the girl's injuries could not have been caused by a single fall from the bed. 

Police said the girl's mother brought the baby to the hospital on Wednesday after she became unresponsive. The woman initially told police the baby became unresponsive while lying face down in their bed after she was fed.

ALABAMA MOM CHARGED WITH MURDER AFTER TODDLER BOUND, LEFT TO SUFFOCATE FOR 12 HOURS: COPS

Prosecutors said the mother told investigators the child was "freezing and in shock" when she took her to the hospital.

Doctors said the baby "suffered from significant head and brain trauma" and "sustained frontal lobe hemorrhaging and a subdural hemorrhage," according to the charging documents.

Hospital staff could not revive the child, and she died in the hospital.

Both parents later admitted to investigators that they noticed the girl's bruises on Sept. 6 and that she began vomiting the following day. They said they did not seek medical treatment until she was unresponsive on Wednesday.

The pair is Guatemalan nationals, and prosecutors argued they pose "an extreme flight risk."

Both parents were held without bail.

item.title: Creepy 'Cat in the Hat' trend targets schools as costumed figure allegedly chases teen girl
item.description: A person dressed as the Cat in the Hat allegedly chased a teen girl in British Columbia as the creepy trend sparks school threats nationwide.
item.content:encoded:
A shadowy figure dressed as the Cat in the Hat allegedly chased a teenage girl through a Canadian neighborhood, as a creepy online trend featuring sinister depictions of the beloved children’s character has prompted investigations and school warnings targeting schools and students across multiple states.

The unidentified girl was walking in West Kelowna, British Columbia, at about 9 p.m. Aug. 24 when a person wearing a costume resembling the Dr. Seuss character allegedly began chasing her, according to the Royal Canadian Mounted Police.

The teen escaped and reached her home safely, but police are still working to identify the costumed individual.

POLICE IDENTIFY SUSPECT ACCUSED OF TERRORIZING PHILADELPHIA WOMEN WHILE WEARING CREEPY CHUCKY-STYLE MASK

"Regardless of whether the individual intended the behavior as a joke, following a young person and causing them to fear for their safety is extremely concerning," Cpl. Devon Gerrits said.

"People should understand that behavior intended as a prank can have serious consequences when it causes another person to reasonably fear for their safety."

TIMELINE REVEALS HOW MAN IN 'CHUCKY' MASK TERRORIZED PHILADELPHIA STREETS, EVADED POLICE

Investigators said wearing a costume is not a crime by itself, but pursuing someone in a way that causes reasonable fear could constitute criminal harassment. Assault, threats or intimidation charges could also be considered depending on the evidence.

Anyone who believes they are being followed or pursued should move toward a populated location, contact a trusted adult and call 911 if they are in immediate danger, the West Kelowna RCMP advised.

Police are asking anyone with doorbell, security or dashcam video taken near the 2000 block of Shamrock Drive at about 9 p.m. Aug. 24 to contact the West Kelowna RCMP.

Police have not said whether the real-world chase is connected to a separate "Cat in the Hat" social media trend that has spread across the United States, putting schools on alert and landing some juveniles in custody.

LOUDOUN COUNTY TRANSGENDER SUBSTITUTE CHARGED WITH MAKING SCHOOL THREATS

The online trend features edited or AI-generated images and videos depicting a sinister version of the Cat in the Hat lurking outside homes, standing near schools or prowling through communities. Some anonymous accounts have added the names of students, staff members, campuses and towns, sometimes accompanied by ominous messages or threats.

Authorities from California to Florida, Virginia and Texas have responded with investigations and increased patrols as they work to separate internet hoaxes from credible dangers.

TIKTOK IN LEGAL HOT SEAT AS STATE ACCUSES APP OF EXPOSING KIDS TO HARMFUL CONTENT WHILE MISLEADING PARENTS

The Baldwin Park Police Department in California said it was reviewing "concerning social media posts" that referenced local schools and named students and staff members.

"Any threat directed toward our schools, students, staff, or community will not be dismissed as a joke or prank," the department warned.

NEW MEXICO SEEKS MASSIVE PENALTY FROM META AFTER JURY FOUND TECH GIANT LIABLE FOR ENDANGERING CHILDREN

Police urged residents not to interact with or recirculate the accounts. Anyone who encounters a threatening post is asked to preserve the content, account name, screenshots, dates and times before reporting it to investigators.

In Virginia, the Hanover County Sheriff’s Office launched an investigation after an account posted content referencing Mechanicsville High School and the trend. Deputies increased their presence at the campus while attempting to identify the person behind the account.

UK TO BAN TIKTOK, YOUTUBE, OTHER SOCIAL MEDIA APPS FOR CHILDREN UNDER 16, STARMER SAYS

The sheriff’s office similarly urged residents not to repost the material, warning that doing so could amplify the message and complicate efforts to trace its origin.

Florida’s St. Johns County Sheriff’s Office said it was investigating content involving county schools but had not identified a credible threat. Deputies nevertheless increased their presence on campuses across the county as a precaution.

Texas law enforcement agencies have also warned that creating or spreading the threatening posts could carry consequences far beyond school discipline.

The Frio County Sheriff’s Office said some anonymous accounts have attached lists of students, schools or communities to menacing images and videos in an apparent attempt to provoke fear.

Authorities there determined posts mentioning the area did not appear to present a credible threat but increased patrols and law enforcement visibility around schools.

"Participating in, re-creating, or spreading these threatening posts is not a harmless joke," the sheriff’s office said, warning that copycat accounts and forwarded threats could lead to charges involving cyberbullying, harassment or terroristic threats.

Laredo police delivered a similar warning, saying criminal charges and arrests may follow even when the person responsible claims the post was only meant as a prank.

GIRL OBSESSED WITH SANDY HOOK, COLUMBINE ALLEGEDLY PLOTTED SCHOOL MASSACRE WITH OTHER STUDENTS: REPORT

"A few seconds on social media can result in a police investigation, school disciplinary action, and potentially serious criminal consequences," the department said.

Premont police met with school district leaders after learning of the trend and warned that fake accounts, AI-generated content and purported pranks involving threats could result in charges including making a terroristic threat or filing a false alarm or report under Texas law.

The warnings come as authorities in multiple states have traced threatening accounts to juveniles.

Four girls between 13 and 15 years old were arrested in Berwick, Louisiana, after police linked them to TikTok accounts that alarmed families and schools, according to Police1. Three were charged with terrorizing or menacing, while a fourth was charged with cyberbullying.

A 12-year-old Florida student was accused of posting a written threat to kill tied to the trend, while a 14-year-old Colorado student was arrested after a post referenced a middle school and several homes, the outlet reported. Authorities in Alabama, Ohio and Kentucky have also announced juvenile arrests or pending charges connected to similar posts.

Police across the affected communities have repeatedly asked parents and students not to share the content, even when attempting to warn others. Instead, users should capture screenshots showing the account name and threatening material and send the evidence directly to school officials or law enforcement.

item.title: Jaxson Dart takes brutal hit early in Giants vs Cowboys opener but what happened next was kind of surprising

Dart didn't get summoned into the blue medical tent.

item.title: New AP Poll Top 25 punishes Ohio State, Oklahoma, Oregon, Texas jumps to No 1 after big comeback
item.description: The AP Top 25 poll reshuffled after Texas Longhorns topped Ohio State, but the Buckeyes' five-spot drop exposes a flaw in how voters weigh losses.
item.content:encoded:
Week two of the college football season delivered another series of typically chaotic results. And the College Football Playoff picture has already shifted, thanks to several surprising outcomes.

The Oregon Ducks were expected to compete for a Big Ten Championship with the Ohio State Buckeyes and Indiana Hoosiers, only to barely escape against Boise State and get deservedly beaten by Oklahoma State. The Cowboys' in-state rivals, the Oklahoma Sooners, lost on the road at Michigan, scoring just 10 points in the process.

Those Wolverines, left for dead after the asterisk-laden win over Western Michigan in week one, are suddenly right back in the playoff picture after beating a top-11 SEC opponent. And of course, the Texas Longhorns won the game of the year over Ohio State, giving them a huge resume boost and a substantial leg up should they need an at-large playoff berth.

This week's AP Top 25 Poll reflects some of that chaos, while also providing a good example of the flaws with the "some wins are better than some losses" perspective shared by such figures as Nick Saban.

Here are this week's rankings, and what it means for the rest of the season.

One of the obvious takeaways? No matter what fans, coaches, or commentators say, it's clear that winning and losing is still king. Even when "strength of schedule" is taken into account.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Oklahoma dropped a whopping 13 spots after losing to Michigan, getting no credit for scheduling a top-20 caliber opponent in a home-and-home series. BYU, meanwhile, jumped a whopping four spots, leapfrogging some teams, after a 28-17 win over Arizona in Provo.

Indiana also moved up after beating up on Howard, as did Miami after a 77-7 win over hapless Florida A&M. Why did those teams move up? Because Ohio State fell a remarkable five spots after a one-point loss on the road to Texas in a game in which they had a 20-point lead and were a missed field goal away from cruising home with a win.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

And therein lies the problem. The Buckeyes did what everyone says they want college football teams to do, scheduled a top-tier opponent in an on-campus series. On the field they lost, but as the postgame win expectancy and expected score indicated, it was effectively an evenly matched game. Per ESPN's SP+, the Longhorns had 50.2% win expectancy, Ohio State, 49.8%. Adjusted scoring margin was 0.0. It's almost impossible to play a more evenly matched game than that.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

Their reward? Falling five spots, behind Indiana and Miami that played overmatched FCS teams. In a world where schedule and resume matters, Ohio State should be no worse than second. They played the now No. 1 team in the country and came as close as you can to winning without winning. Why did they drop at all? It's not as if their win over Ball State wasn't impressive, or that we've learned something about Georgia after the Bulldogs played Tennessee State and Western Kentucky.

Human beings, no matter what they say or claim, will always evaluate based on results. It's too much to ask for them to move teams up or down based on other factors. So the Buckeyes and Sooners drop, and playing an FCS team is rewarded.

At the end of the day and season, week two of the AP Poll doesn't matter much. But it's indicative of the mindset that the playoff selection committee has and will have. It's not just wins and losses, it's how you play against the competition you face.

As for Oregon, they have the schedule and talent to fight their way back into playoff contention, but their margin for error is now gone. After Portland State, they travel to USC, and still have Ohio State, Michigan, and Washington later in the season. The Ducks better kick things into high gear sooner rather than later, or by the end of September they could be on the outside of the top 25 looking in.

item.title: Missing 70-year-old hiker rescued after disappearing for a week in remote national park
item.description: A Coast Guard helicopter crew hoisted Craig Berg to safety after he went missing for a week while hiking in Michigan’s remote Isle Royale National Park.
item.content:encoded:
A 70-year-old man who vanished a week ago while hiking in Isle Royale National Park was found "alive and alert" Saturday, according to officials.

Craig Berg was suffering from hypothermia when he was rescued by Coast Guard and Michigan State Police crews, officials said.

"The Coast Guard and Michigan State Police rescued an injured, ailing man Saturday after he went missing in Isle Royale National Park on Sept. 5," the U.S. Coast Guard Great Lakes said.

Video released by authorities shows a helicopter crew from Coast Guard Air Station Traverse City hoisting Berg from the ground. He was then taken to a regional airport in Gwinn for emergency medical evaluation.

MISSOURI DEPUTY AG, MISSING 6 DAYS AFTER SEEKING TO SUMMIT WYOMING'S TALLEST PEAK, IS FOUND ALIVE

Officials did not disclose what happened to Berg while he was missing or provide additional details about his injuries.

Berg was spotted by "good Samaritan" backpackers in the park Saturday before Michigan State Police foot patrols and K-9 units reached him, according to officials.

Multiple agencies and resources were deployed to aid the emergency search, which also included a 45-foot Coast Guard boat, drones and seaplanes.

The search involved the National Park Service, Michigan Department of Natural Resources, Keweenaw County Sheriff’s Office, Wisconsin State Patrol and Minnesota Department of Public Safety, according to Lt. Ben Eckola, a Michigan State Police public information officer.

"We’re also thankful to the fellow hikers who helped, Isle Royale Seaplanes, and No One Left Behind K9 Search and Rescue. Everyone’s efforts played an important part in finding Craig," Eckola said in a statement.

ILLINOIS MAN MISSING MORE THAN A WEEK AS CREWS SCOUR GREAT SMOKY MOUNTAINS NATIONAL PARK

The Detroit Free Press reported that Berg, of Royal Oak, Michigan, arrived at the national park on Aug. 27 for an extended solo hike but failed to return home Sept. 5.

Isle Royale National Park is located on a remote island in Lake Superior near the Canadian border.

Due to its remote location, Isle Royale is one of the least-visited national parks and has limited infrastructure.

Berg’s wife, Debbie, told the Detroit Free Press that only two rangers are stationed on the island and that the park has two camp stores and a lodge.

According to the park’s website, cell phone service is often "unreliable," and many types of equipment are generally prohibited on the island, including bicycles, motorized vehicles and drones.

House shows are untelevised events that occur outside of the main shows that WWE holds each week. Usually, champions put their titles on the line or have matches against rivals with little to no consequence to the storylines they’re telling when fans tune in on Mondays, Tuesdays and Fridays.

item.title: Accused killers vanish after family massacre before manhunt ends hundreds of miles away
item.description: A deadly North Carolina shooting left two dead and two critically injured before suspects Camryn Moore and Cory Armstrong fled across state lines.
item.content:encoded:
A deadly shooting inside a North Carolina family home triggered an urgent search for two accused killers and an interstate manhunt that would end with another burst of gunfire.

Gaston County Police officers responded to a home on Forbes Road at approximately 8:43 a.m. Thursday after receiving a report of gunfire inside the residence.

Officers discovered four people suffering from gunshot wounds. Two were pronounced dead at the scene, while two others were rushed to CaroMont Regional Medical Center with life-threatening injuries.

Police identified the two people killed as Victoria "Heather" Moore, 50, and Megan "Josiah" Bumgardner, 38. The two surviving victims remained in critical but stable condition Friday, according to police.

4 SHOT INSIDE NORTH CAROLINA HOME, 2 KILLED AS POLICE IDENTIFY PERSON OF INTEREST

Detectives identified two residents of the home, Camryn Moore, 26, and Cory Armstrong, 29, as suspects in the bloodshed. WSOC-TV reported that Heather Moore was Camryn Moore’s mother and Bumgardner was her uncle.

Police said they believed everyone involved knew one another and described the shooting as an isolated incident with no continuing threat to the Gaston County community.

Investigators have not disclosed what may have triggered the violence.

Camryn Moore and Armstrong allegedly fled Gaston County immediately after the shooting. By Thursday afternoon, detectives had obtained warrants charging each of them with two counts of first-degree murder and two counts of attempted first-degree murder.

WATCH: DEPUTIES HUNT WANTED MAN THROUGH CORNFIELD AFTER HIGH-SPEED CHASE CAUGHT ON CAMERA

The Gaston County Police Department enlisted the help of the U.S. Marshals Service Carolinas Regional Fugitive Task Force as investigators tracked the pair’s movements across multiple states overnight.

SUSPECTED HUMAN SMUGGLERS LEAD COPS ON 100-MPH CHASE BEFORE BAILING AND ALLEGEDLY COMMITTING ARMED CARJACKING

The search reached Ohio at approximately 8 a.m. Friday, when state troopers spotted the suspects’ vehicle outside Athens and attempted to pull it over, authorities said.

Moore and Armstrong allegedly refused to stop, setting off a multi-county pursuit.

The chase came to a violent end when their vehicle swerved to avoid spike strips deployed in the roadway and crashed, according to information provided to North Carolina investigators by Ohio authorities.

Officers then reported hearing two gunshots coming from the wrecked vehicle.

Law enforcement deployed a drone to look inside and discovered Moore and Armstrong dead. Authorities have not disclosed who fired the shots or officially announced the manner of their deaths.

The Ohio State Highway Patrol is investigating the pursuit, crash and deaths.

Back in Gastonia, neighbors were stunned by the violence that shattered their normally peaceful street.

Loretta Forbes, whose husband’s grandfather built her home in 1914 and gave Forbes Road its name, told WSOC-TV that she knew the family living next door.

"I just kept saying, ‘My God. Oh God,’ coming down the stairs," Forbes told the outlet. "They seem to be very nice people. It just shakes you up to think that could happen so close by."

Forbes said she was praying for the family and searching for answers.

"I want to know what’s happened," she said. "I want to know about the family."

Jennifer Greene, a friend and co-worker of Heather Moore, drove to the home after Moore unexpectedly failed to report for her shift.

SUSPECTED DUI DRIVER LEADS COPS ON WILD CHASE BEFORE DRAMATIC TAKEDOWN ON POPULAR CALIFORNIA BEACH

"This was a tragic act of violence that resulted in the loss of multiple lives and left others critically injured," the Gaston County Police Department said.

"Although the search for the suspects has ended, our investigation has not," police added.

Anyone with information about the shooting is asked to contact Detective G. Lancaster at 704-866-3320 or CrimeStoppers at 704-861-8000.

item.title: Anthropic CEO likens AI fight with China to Cold War, seeks 'disarmament negotiations'
item.description: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei compared the AI race with China to Cold War nuclear tensions, urging arms limitation-style talks to slow growing technology.
item.content:encoded:
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei on Sunday compared the U.S.-China artificial intelligence (AI) race to the Cold War with the Soviet Union, warning both nations must manage the threat of "potential destruction" from each other.

Amodei, who previously published an essay on Saturday warning about AI efforts outpacing human capabilities to control the technology, reiterated his concerns to "CBS Sunday Morning" that AI could potentially threaten mankind if left unchecked. He encouraged efforts to slow down production, but CBS correspondent Jo Ling Kent asked him whether that was the best solution to compete with China.

Amodei acknowledged that it was a tough "dilemma" for the U.S. but suggested that part of the solution could be to open discussions with China as the U.S. did with the Soviet Union.

MIKE JOHNSON REJECTS AI MORATORIUM OVER CHINA THREAT AS CONSERVATIVE ACTIVIST DEMANDS GUARDRAILS

"It's not in any government's interest to have bioterrorism," Amodei said. "And so we should talk with the Chinese and see if we can work together to put limits to put a speed limit on the rate of this technology."

"It's a little bit like, you know, for all our differences with, you know, other systems of government and I have many — I generally have a hawkish position on China —but for all our differences, think about when it was the U.S. and the Soviet Union, right?" he continued. "And we each had 10,000 nuclear missiles pointed at each other. Even for all our differences, we recognized that that was too many, that we needed to engage in talks that could lower the scale of the potential destruction."

Kent asked whether he believed the Cold War should be used as a model for the AI arms race.

CHINA IS BUILDING AN AI WAR MACHINE. WASHINGTON MUST WAKE UP BEFORE IT’S TOO LATE

"I didn't say we should use the Cold War as a model...disarmament negotiations like arms limitation, I do think that is an appropriate lens through which to think about this at the geopolitical level," Amodei said. "If we look at what AI models can do in terms of cyber, like they absolutely have geopolitical and national security significance. Of course, they do. That's why we're having this whole conversation."

Fox News Digital reached out to Anthropic for comment.

Amodei's essay drew support from high-profile tech executives such as SpaceX CEO and xAI founder Elon Musk and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman. However, other tech experts and entrepreneurs disagreed with his essay, either because of his concerns or his suggestions.

Former White House AI "czar" David Sacks pushed back against AI warnings like Amodei's, including a viral post from former Anthropic staffer Jacob Coxon.

FETTERMAN ALIGNS WITH TRUMP ON AI PUSH, WARNS CHINA BENEFITS FROM US 'OVERREACTION'

"[The warnings are] designed to scare the public about AI so that these NGOs can implement their preferred approach to AI, which is a government takeover," Sacks told "Special Report" on Thursday.

Former OpenAI researcher Daniel Kokotajlo responded to Amodei's essay on "Fox News Live" Saturday, arguing that voluntary industry measures might not be enough to prevent advanced systems from escaping human control.

"After they've accumulated all of the hard power in the world, they run the factories, they're integrated into the military, you know, they're sort of running the whole system, and humans are just sort of giving them orders," Kokotajlo said. "Then they stop taking orders at some points, and they kill off the humans."

The island's capture came after a month-long offensive along Yemen’s western coast that killed more than 1,500 soldiers and forced Yemen’s government to acknowledge a "painful" defeat, according to The Associated Press.

"With Perim, they have gained what we could call the cork in the Red Sea bottle," Morgan Murphy, a former Pentagon press secretary and retired Navy captain, told Fox News Digital.

"But they've put themselves into a kill box. They're nowhere near the capability of the United States and if the president so chooses, he can wipe them off the face of that rock pretty easily," Murphy warned.

SAUDI ARABIA TELLS TRUMP NOW IS THE TIME FOR MILITARY ACTION AS IRAN-BACKED HOUTHIS ADVANCE

Despite Perim sitting in the middle of the narrow maritime passage, Murphy detailed how the Houthis had effectively placed themselves in an area that is vulnerable to concentrated fire.

"Perim cuts that chokepoint right in half, and it's only 18 miles wide there," Murphy said.

He said the island has served as a pivotal maritime vantage point for hundreds of years, previously targeted for control by French forces and held by the British Empire for over a century.

Perim — a desolate volcanic island also known as Mayun — also sits roughly 20 miles off the Horn of Africa, placing it in proximity to Camp Lemonnier in Djibouti, home to one of the largest U.S. military installations on the continent.

"We have incredible firepower in that region, and that's a little rock in the middle of that strait. It's a volcanic rock. It doesn't have any water. It's uninhabitable," Murphy warned.

"There's no vegetation to speak of. And the Houthis have just massed their troops on that rock. So what that is, what we would call that in the Navy, is a kill box."

Satellite imagery of the island shows a 1.85-kilometer (6,070-foot) runway alongside three military hangars, which regional intelligence reports attribute to past construction by the United Arab Emirates.

"There's a 6,000-foot airstrip on that island. I think that Emiratis built it," Murphy said.

‘GATE OF TEARS’ AT RISK: IRAN THREATENS MAJOR NEW GLOBAL CHOKEPOINT IF US MOVES ON HORMUZ

"It's nice to have an airstrip, and especially a long runway, but we don't know the condition of that runway. We don't know how they could possibly use that runway, and they certainly don't have the sophisticated air power that the United States and its allies have to project power from that runway."

He added that the U.S. military holds overwhelming force options if commanders elect to target the island.

"We could wipe that rock into glass, just blast it into a smooth glass surface, put skates back on our feet, and skate all over it," Murphy said.

"That's why the Houthis have kind of played coy with the president, and they know that even if they fortify that rock they're not going to be able to hold it in the face of the United States Navy."

The developments come amid diplomatic maneuvering between Washington, Riyadh and the Houthis in recent days.

Sources confirmed to Fox News Digital that Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman had called President Donald Trump twice Sept. 10 to urge him to authorize U.S. military strikes against Houthi positions.

Trump declined direct intervention, with U.S. officials noting the administration has no immediate plans for direct combat involvement but will continue offering intelligence assistance.

IRAN AND HOUTHI TERROR PROXY FACING RED SEA THREAT FROM PRO-US AFRICAN NATION

Speaking to reporters in Dublin on Sept. 12, Trump also indicated the Houthis had signaled a desire to avoid direct confrontation with American forces.

"The Houthis called us, and they don’t want to fight with us. They let us know, they don’t want to fight with us... they don’t want us to go after them," Trump said.

Murphy suggested, however, that Washington’s restraint should not be mistaken for inaction.

"I can't speak for the president. But this administration has not shown a lack of resolve to use force," Murphy said.

"I wouldn't doubt at all if the president took steps to pound some of these folks into the sand if they continue to really disrupt the global energy supply."

Yemeni government, regional and Iranian sources told Reuters the Houthi advance was sustained by Iranian weaponry and tactical direction from the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, or IRGC, with U.S. officials estimating hundreds of IRGC officers remain active in Yemen.

Murphy noted that Tehran's strategy appears designed to drive up global fuel prices by choking critical shipping lanes.

TRUMP THREATENS 'MAJOR MILITARY PUNISHMENT' FOR IRAN OVER FUTURE HOUTHI ATTACKS

Comparing the conflict to historical naval power struggles, Murphy emphasized the strategic mismatch.

"We're in a different era. They are nowhere near the sophistication of the world's major powers. The Houthis are using a 19th-century playbook. They are not using 21st-century warfare," he said.

"So, yes, they've caught a critical cork in the Red Sea bottle, but how they use it remains to be seen," Murphy concluded.

"This is an example of why great powers really have to have a strong Navy. This is why Great Britain had a strong navy. This is why the United States has a strong navy, because there's so many regional powers who want to try to bottle up shipping, whether it is in the Strait of Malacca, whether it is in the Strait of Hormuz, and here, in this case, in the Red Sea."

"I think what we're going to see in the next several days and weeks is a coordinated effort by the Trump administration to make sure our allies are on board in helping us keep these critical waterways open, free, and clear for freedom of navigation," he said.

item.title: Ben Shelton loses in US Open final to Zverev, but America has found its next big men's tennis star
item.description: Alexander Zverev beat Ben Shelton 6-3, 7-6, 5-7, 6-2 to win the US Open, but the 23-year-old American's fight showed why fans can't wait to watch him.
item.content:encoded:
Let’s get the obvious part out of the way immediately: This stinks.

Ben Shelton had a chance to end a 23-year Grand Slam drought for American men’s tennis on Sunday afternoon in New York. Instead, Alexander Zverev beat him 6-3, 7-6 (2), 5-7, 6-2 to win the U.S. Open and capture his second Grand Slam title of the year.

American men’s tennis missed a golden opportunity, but Shelton gave America a tennis star worth rooting for.

It's not the same as winning, but it's a major positive step for a country desperate to find the next great American player.

Shelton, making his first career Grand Slam final appearance, looked nervous from the start. The first game told us exactly what kind of afternoon this might be.

He committed two errors to give Zverev an immediate break point, then double-faulted to hand over the break in the first game of the match. Shelton double-faulted again on set point to drop the opening set, 6-3.

LADIES AT THE US OPEN WERE CAUGHT ON CAMERA TAKING NOTICE OF A SHIRTLESS CARLOS ALCARAZ

The second set played out on even terms until the tiebreak, which is where Shelton’s game fell apart. Zverev raced to a 5-0 lead and took it 7-2.

Zverev wasn’t blowing Shelton off the court, which is what made the match so frustrating to watch. Shelton kept getting into winnable points on Zverev’s serve, only to miss a forehand, dump a backhand into the net or choose the wrong shot at the wrong moment.

For most of the match, Shelton looked like the more gifted player. His power, athleticism and creativity are fun to watch. The 23-year-old American produced most of the shots that made the crowd gasp and his serve regularly crossed 140 mph. His flashes of greatness showed that he's much more than another American man with a big serve.

But the inconsistency killed his chances to win his first Grand Slam title.

Zverev didn’t need to be spectacular. He served well, kept the ball in play and waited for Shelton to crack. Steady isn’t particularly exciting, but it wins Grand Slam finals when the guy on the other side keeps giving away points. And Zverev's win at the French Open earlier this summer gave him a crucial edge in experience that showed up throughout the match.

Still, Shelton didn’t go quietly.

He finally earned his first break point of the match with Zverev serving at 2-3 in the third set, but the German erased it. Shelton kept holding, waited for another chance and pounced with Zverev serving at 5-6. He jumped ahead 0-40 and converted his second set point when Zverev missed a routine volley.

So, Shelton had life.

Then he immediately put himself in trouble again. Shelton led 30-0 in his opening service game of the fourth set before a double fault and another forehand error opened the door. He saved one break point with a gutsy serve-and-volley play, but Zverev eventually broke and never gave it back.

That was essentially the match. Zverev broke Shelton again at 4-2 before serving out the match in the final game. There was a funny moment at the very end, as Zverev didn't realize he had just won the U.S. Open.

After a Shelton return went long, Zverev appeared to think there was more tennis to play. He went to serve again before realizing the match was over and he was the champion. At that point, a huge smile crept over his face and he threw his arms in the air.

On the other side, a clearly frustrated Ben Shelton appeared to be holding back his emotions as he went to shake his opponent's hand.

This was the opportunity.

World No. 1 Jannik Sinner withdrew prior to the tournament because of a knee injury. Novak Djokovic lost in the first round. Shelton stunned defending champion Carlos Alcaraz in a five-set quarterfinal that ended at 3:33 in the morning.

The three biggest obstacles were gone and Shelton was responsible for eliminating one of them.

US OPEN WINNER ANDY RODDICK DEFENDS LATE FINISHES AMID CRITICISM AFTER BEN SHELTON-CARLOS ALCARAZ THRILLER

Zverev was hardly an easy opponent. He won the French Open in June, reached the Wimbledon final and entered Sunday having beaten Shelton in all five of their previous meetings.

Now the 29-year-old owns two major championships.

Over the past 30 years, only seven other men have won multiple Grand Slam titles in the same calendar year: Pete Sampras, Andre Agassi, Roger Federer, Rafael Nadal, Novak Djokovic, Carlos Alcaraz and Sinner.

That’s elite company.

Zverev’s off-the-court legacy is more complicated. He has faced domestic abuse allegations from two former partners, both of which he has denied. The ATP closed an investigation into one set of allegations in 2023 after finding insufficient evidence to substantiate the claims, and a German court closed a separate case in 2024 after a settlement with no finding or admission of guilt.

On the court, there’s no longer any debate about whether Zverev can handle the final Sunday of a major. He proved it in Paris and did it again in New York.

But this was still a winnable final for Shelton. Since Andy Roddick won the 2003 U.S. Open, American men have gone 0-for-7 in Grand Slam finals. Roddick accounted for four of those losses, while Andre Agassi, Taylor Fritz and now Shelton each fell once.

American men’s tennis couldn’t have asked for a clearer path to ending the drought. It still couldn’t finish the job and, because of that, it's a failure.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Of course, ESPN immediately tried to turn Shelton’s run into a story about race.

"It’s more than just Ben Shelton’s first U.S. Open Final," the network posted after his semifinal victory.

ESPN then noted that Shelton was the first Black American man to reach the U.S. Open final since Arthur Ashe in 1972. That’s historically accurate.

But Shelton never made this run about his skin color. The media wanted to put him in that box, and he didn’t follow them there.

He’s an American. That’s what mattered.

Shelton has consistently used his platform to talk about his Christian faith, his family and his country. After winning in Australia earlier this year, he signed a television camera with the message, "USA ’til it’s backwards."

After beating Alcaraz in the biggest victory of his career, Shelton immediately pointed to his faith.

"I’m just so grateful, so blessed. God’s blessed me in so many ways," Shelton said.

He made a similar point after winning in Montreal earlier this summer, saying, "I would be nowhere without my faith. That’s what’s most important to me."

Then came Friday’s semifinal against Frances Tiafoe, played on the 25th anniversary of the Sept. 11, 2001, terrorist attacks.

Shelton spoke about the sacrifices his parents made and dedicated the victory to his late grandmother. He asked the New York crowd to return for the final because, as he put it, "We’re going for it here."

"Do this for the USA," Shelton said.

Before leaving the court, completely unprompted, Shelton offered his thoughts and prayers to the families affected by 9/11 and called New York one of the greatest cities in the world.

That’s the guy America has watched for the past two weeks.

He’s powerful, emotional and wildly entertaining. He also loves his family, talks openly about God and treats representing the United States as an honor, not a burden.

Now, let’s not pretend losing a Grand Slam final is the same as winning one because it isn't. Ben Shelton will be the first one to say that, too. He had the chance American men’s tennis had been waiting more than two decades to get, and he didn’t finish the job.

But Shelton’s tournament was still a massive win for him and for American tennis.

He beat Carlos Alcaraz and reached his first Grand Slam final. He had a chance to give up against Zverev, but he kept fighting and forced a fourth set. He showed the composure, faith and love of country that make American sports fans want to invest in a player.

Shelton didn’t deliver America a trophy on Sunday.

But he gave us a tennis star we can’t wait to watch try again.

item.title: Dolph Lundgren and wife Emma Krokdal enjoy date night at Arnold Schwarzenegger’s charity event

item.title: Jeremiyah Love makes immediate statement with touchdown on first career drive in Cardinals' upset win
item.description: Jeremiyah Love's NFL debut featured a statement touchdown as the Arizona Cardinals opened their season against the Los Angeles Chargers at SoFi Stadium.
item.content:encoded:
Jeremiyah Love’s NFL career started off on quite the high note during the Arizona Cardinals’ Week 1 match-up against the Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday.

Love immediately became one of the highest-paid running backs in the NFL when the Cardinals took him third overall back in April out of Notre Dame.

As a result, the expectations were quite high for Love given his draft stock, which tagged him as one of the faces of not just the franchise’s future, but the league as a whole.

Love and the Cardinals took the field at SoFi Stadium as underdogs against the Chargers, but an opening drive by quarterback Jacoby Brissett and Arizona’s offense led to a red-zone opportunity that their new running back didn’t squander.

Arizona, which was a 10-point underdog, defeated the Chargers 26-14. 

On second-and-goal from the Chargers’ 5-yard line, Love got the handoff from Brissett, bounced out to his left, and found a lane to the left pylon and didn’t lose sight of it. Love outraced the Chargers' defender closing in on him, and he scored his first career touchdown in a statement drive from the Cardinals to begin the season.

JEREMIYAH LOVE SIGNS ROOKIE DEAL THAT GIVES HIM MOST GUARANTEED MONEY BY RUNNING BACK BEFORE TAKING NFL SNAP

Love finished with 41 yards on 11 carries. 

First-year head coach Mike LaFleur was visibly enthusiastic after the 70-yard opening drive, joining his players in celebration, Love among them. It’s hard not to love (no pun intended) what this dynamic running back can bring his offense in 2026 and beyond.

The Cardinals caught some flak for the pick of Love when they put in their ticket in April. Arizona is a rebuilding team, one that fired ex-head coach Jonathan Gannon and hired LaFleur with the goal of getting the team back on the right track.

With a pick of Love at third overall, it signaled to some that the Cardinals believed they were one offensive weapon away from competing for a playoff berth. On the other hand, the Cardinals need more playmakers on both sides of the ball, and Love did just that during his stellar collegiate career for the Fighting Irish.

Love dealt with an ankle injury throughout training camp, too, which begged the question of how much he’d play for LaFleur in Week 1. Love split carries with veteran Tyler Allgeier, whom Arizona brought in this offseason as a free agent acquisition.

item.title: Josh Allen torches one of NFL's best defenses to make case it's time to move on from 2025 playoff loss
item.description: Josh Allen passed for 334 yards, threw 2 TDs and ran for 2 others as the Buffalo Bills scored 36 points against an elite Houston Texans defense.
item.content:encoded:
Josh Allen finished last season in tears and the sight of one of the NFL's great players sobbing in the Buffalo Bills locker room after a playoff loss to the Denver Broncos led ownership to fire head coach Sean McDermott. That memory of that scene and the burden it put on Allen was buried on Sunday.

Josh Allen played sensationally against the Houston Texans in a stirring 36-31 game this day. And this means stuff:

It means new Bills coach Joe Brady won his head coaching debut.

It means the Bills have just sent the NFL the message that they remain a Super Bowl contender for 2026 because, well, the Texans team they just beat are a Super Bowl contender.

And it means Josh Allen has already joined the MVP race in earnest after he exorcised the ghosts of his horrible postseason performance and that loss which haunted all offseason.

Allen also made the statement that he can indeed play up to his standard even against the Texans.

"We do like Reliant Stadium, woo-hoo!" Allen exclaimed after the game. "It feels good. It feels good to start the season off right. Obviously coach Joe getting his first win as an NFL head coach ... really happy for him. [He] called a heck of a game."

JOSH ALLEN DELIVERS FULL-THROATED UNSOLICITED DEFENSE OF BUFFALO BILLS' HIDEOUS NEW UNIFORMS

The Texans had dominated Allen in five previous games. The Texans won four of those and limited Allen to 196 passing yards per game.

Not this game.

Allen played up to his billing this time. He played like he's one of the league's best players.

He passed for 334 yards and two touchdowns. And he rushed for two touchdowns. Allen was in some way responsible for all four of his team's touchdowns, by either running or passing for them.

Amid all those numbers, Allen tried to put the focus on others.

"It's the players that we got, man," Allen said in his postgame interview with CBS.

"Looking down at these stats, man, our guys made some great plays."

Don't believe Allen. He delivered superstar stuff against the defense that was the NFL's best against the pass last year and was second-best in points allowed behind only the Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks.

Translation: Houston dominates on defense.

And Allen dominated Houston as the Bills scored the most points that defense has allowed since 2023.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

"We scored 36 points against a fantastic defense," Allen said. "However you get to 36 points in the NFL, you'll take that any other week. As long as it's more than the other guys."

Allen smiling and joking after this game is quite a different snapshot than the one we got from him in his previous game – that playoff loss to the Broncos. Allen turned the ball four times in that fateful game.

He fumbled twice, and threw two interceptions, including interception that set up the Broncos' game-winning drive.

Allen hasn't said he lost that game for the Bills, but he has taken responsibility for it. And whether he did lose it or not, the NFL narrative that Allen couldn't get his team into the Super Bowl grew.

It's impossible to make the case this was a big game on par with the playoffs. But in recording his 26th game-winning drive in the fourth quarter or overtime – the most in the league since 2018 – Allen reminded everyone that he's over that past disappointment.

And in this new season he gets another shot at the Super Bowl.

item.title: Trump unloads on AOC, Mamdani for laughing during sacred 9/11 ceremony at Ground Zero
item.description: President Donald Trump called the moment "terrible" after video showed AOC and Zohran Mamdani appearing to laugh during the Ground Zero ceremony.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump slammed Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez and New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani for appearing to laugh during the solemn reading of victims’ names at the 9/11 Memorial, calling their behavior "terrible" and "inappropriate."

"I think it’s terrible," Trump said when asked about the video of the two Democrats. "It’s not a place to be laughing, especially in that case."

"I thought it was terrible," he continued. "The fact that they were laughing together at a very important part of the ceremony was inappropriate."

The president’s condemnation came after video of Ocasio-Cortez and Mamdani sharing what appeared to be a lighthearted exchange at Ground Zero sparked widespread criticism online.

AOC, MAMDANI INTERACTION CAUGHT ON CAM AT 9/11 MEMORIAL SPARKS ONLINE FURY

A television feed from Friday’s ceremony showed a young man overcome with emotion near the memorial before cutting to Mamdani and Ocasio-Cortez smiling and appearing to laugh as they spoke. Their conversation could not be heard.

9/11 WIDOW TERRY STRADA ACCUSES US OF PROTECTING SAUDI ARABIA 25 YEARS AFTER TERROR ATTACKS, ADDRESSES VANCE

The moment unfolded as mourners read aloud the names of those killed in the Sept. 11, 2001, terrorist attacks and the 1993 World Trade Center bombing during ceremonies marking the 25th anniversary of 9/11. Nearly 3,000 people were killed in the 2001 attacks.

The video quickly spread across social media, where critics accused the pair of showing disrespect on one of the nation’s most solemn days.

MAMDANI DRAWS FURY FROM 9/11 MOURNERS OVER GROUND ZERO APPEARANCE: ‘DISRESPECTFUL’

"As the names of Americans murdered on September 11th are read aloud at Ground Zero, AOC and Mamdani are laughing and smiling together," Rep. Wesley Hunt, R-Texas, wrote on X.

"There is a time and a place for politics. This isn’t it. Ground Zero is sacred ground," Hunt added. "September 11 is not a photo op, it is not a networking event."

MAMDANI HEADS TO 9/11 MEMORIAL DESPITE 110,000-SIGNATURE PUSH FROM VICTIMS’ FAMILIES TO STAY AWAY

Meghan McCain also reacted to the video, asking on X, "Why the f--- are these two laughing?"

New York City Councilwoman Inna Vernikov, a Republican, similarly ripped the moment.

ZOHRAN MAMDANI URGED TO SKIP NEW YORK CITY'S 9/11 MEMORIAL: 'VILE ANTISEMITE'

"After thousands of families of victims of terror beg Mamdani not to show up, he stands there and laughs while families weep," Vernikov wrote. "This is NYC’s Mayor."

Mamdani had already faced opposition from some victims’ families ahead of the ceremony. A petition urging him to stay away from Ground Zero gathered more than 110,000 signatures, though Mamdani attended and remained for the ceremony.

DE NIRO CALLS CONTROVERSIAL MAMDANI POLICE COMMENTS 'RIDICULOUS' AS HE DEFENDS MAYOR GOING TO 9/11 SERVICE

However, Michael Ragusa, who has served as a member of former New York City Mayor Rudy Giuliani’s entourage, disputed claims that Mamdani and Ocasio-Cortez were joking about the ceremony.

"The videos of [them] laughing are not true. I was standing next to them the whole time," Ragusa wrote on X.

MS RACHEL DEFENDS 'AWESOME' MAMDANI AMID 9/11 MEMORIAL CONTROVERSY, SAYS HE'S VICTIM OF ISLAMOPHOBIC ATTACKS

"The camera just caught her greeting him hello," he added. "Multiple other politicians were laughing and joking behind me. Republicans and Democrats."

Mamdani was seen standing somberly at other points during the ceremony. It remains unclear what he and Ocasio-Cortez discussed during the brief exchange.

Fox News Digital previously reached out to Mamdani and Ocasio-Cortez for comment.

Fox News Digital's Charles Creitz contributed to this report.

item.title: Kyler Murray knocked out of Vikings debut after forearm to the helmet and blow to neck by two Packers
item.description: Kyler Murray left the Vikings' home opener after a brutal hit from Lukas Van Ness and Javon Bullard sent triggered the NFL concussion protocol.
item.content:encoded:
That start of Kyler Murray's career with the Minnesota Vikings has been a disaster.

That might be understating the matter.

The team's new starting quarterback threw an interception on the second play of the regular-season opener. It was his first pass in a Vikings uniform.

At home, no less.

MINNESOTA VIKINGS SURPRISINGLY DEMOTE FORMER FIRST-ROUND PICK JJ MCCARTHY TO THIRD STRING

Then Murray got knocked out of the game on his team's third possession.

Murray, signed by the Vikings in the offseason as their next major quarterback project, did not make it out of the first quarter on Sunday.

Murray left the game and underwent a concussion evaluation. He was listed officially as questionable to return, though the severity of the hit made clear to those watching that his day was over.

The Vikings eventually ruled Murray out.

"Definitely, thinking about Kyler," Vikings receiver Justin Jefferson said, "Definitely prayers out to him. Definitely don't want to see one of our brothers go down with that type of injury."

Murray was scrambling when he took a forearm to the helmet from Packers defensive end Lukas Van Ness, but that wasn't all.

As Murray collapsed in a heap, he took another blow from safety Javon Bullard around the neck and head area, causing Murray's helmet to fly off.

And he seemed to go into a fencing response position, which is an involuntary body posture where an injured person extends one arm rigidly and flexes the other into the air for several seconds after a blow to the head.

Carson Wentz took over for Murray after the play, and led Minnesota to a 39-22 victory.

Murray will enter the NFL concussion protocol. That means he will be tested, and independent physicians will determine when he can eventually return to play.

For a player experiencing his first concussion, the standard return-to-play timeline is roughly two weeks, though absences of one week or three weeks are not uncommon.

Coach Kevin O'Connell said afterward he saw Murray and the quarterback "seemed to be doing pretty well, but I wouldn't medically quote me on that."

So, yes. It's been a terrible start to the season, and his Vikings career, for Murray.
